The Stable Log Pseudo-Determinant and Its Derivative Blocks

Source: R/additive_penalty.R
additive_stable.Rd

Evaluates \(\log\mathrm{pdet}\sum_k\lambda_kP_k\) together with \(\operatorname{tr}(S^{+}P_k)\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(S^{+}P_kS^{+}P_l)\) by the similarity transformation that additive_sum() describes. The function recurses on the Schur complement, so it handles any number of components.

Usage

additive_stable(mats, lam, p_rank, d_tol = additive_tol(), r_tol = 1e-10)

Arguments

mats

The component matrices, as AdditivePenalty() stores them.

lam

The smoothing parameters, in the same order.

p_rank

The rank of the sum, fixed at construction.

d_tol

The threshold at which the components are split, additive_tol() by default.

r_tol

The relative eigenvalue tolerance at which the rank of a group is counted, 1e-10 by default. additive_sum() passes the tol stored in the AdditivePenalty() object, which is the tolerance at which additive_penalty() counted the rank of the sum.

Value

A list of value (a single number), dlog (a numeric vector), d2log (a square matrix) and depth (the number of levels of the partition, a diagnostic).

Details

The rank of a group of components is counted on the sum of its components after each has been divided by its largest absolute entry, and never on the weighted sum. additive_penalty() counts the rank of the whole penalty in the same way and at the same tolerance. The null space of a sum of positive semidefinite matrices is the intersection of their null spaces, so the rank of a group is a property of that group and is counted without the spread of the parameters. The rank passed to the next level is the current rank less the rank of the dominant group, so it is obtained by subtraction and never counted again.

A level returns NaN for the value and for both derivative blocks when its weighted sum or reduction is not finite, when the Cholesky factorization of \(A\) fails, or, at the last level, when the smallest of the eigenvalues that are kept is not positive; a NaN at a deeper level is passed up.

See also

additive_sum(), which calls it and checks its result.
